script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

TITLE: THE MEMORY PALACE

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

A small, cluttered living room filled with old photographs, books, and trinkets. JOANNA (50s), a professional violinist with long, curly brown hair, sits on the couch, her eyes glued to a picture of her late husband, JASON (40s), smiling back at her.

JOANNA
(whispers)
I'll never forget you.

The phone rings. Joanna hesitates, then answers.

JOANNA
(into phone)
Hello?

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

A bustling coffee shop filled with the sounds of clinking cups and chatter. CHARLIE (30s), a shy but determined young man, nervously twists a paper napkin as he waits for his meeting with Joanna.

CHARLIE
(voiceover)
I've practiced this speech a hundred times. But what if I mess it up?

A WAITRESS places a cup of coffee in front of Charlie, startling him.

WAITRESS
For you, sir.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Joanna picks up the phone.

JOANNA
(into phone)
Hello? Yes, this is Joanna.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Charlie gulps down a deep breath and stands up as Joanna enters, looking more put-together than he expected.

CHARLIE
(nervously)
Ms. Green, I'm Charlie. I'm here to talk about your late husband, Jason.

Joanna looks surprised but composed as they walk out of the coffee shop together.

EXT. PARK - DAY

They sit on a bench, surrounded by the vibrant colors of the park.

CHARLIE
(nervously)
I've been researching memory palaces for years. I believe I can help you remember things you've forgotten, like the details of Jason's last days.

JOANNA
(skeptical)
How can you possibly do that?

CHARLIE
I've created a memory palace for your memories. A place where they're safe, accessible, and can be remembered clearly.

INT. MEMORY PALACE - INTERIOR - DAY

The memory palace is a large, open space filled with memories, each one a room. Joanna and Charlie walk through, exploring the rooms filled with memories of Jason.

INT. KITCHEN - MEMORY PALACE

They enter a kitchen where Joanna and Jason are laughing as they cook dinner together.

JOANNA
(smiling)
I hadn't remembered this. It feels so real.

CHARLIE
The memories are real. They're just hidden away, waiting to be found.

INT. BEDROOM - MEMORY PALACE

They enter a bedroom where Jason sits up in bed, looking tired but hopeful as he tells Joanna about his new job opportunity.

CHARLIE
You've forgotten this detail, but I remember it clearly. He was excited about the new job, but he was also worried about the long hours and the impact it would have on your family.

INT. HOSPITAL ROOM - MEMORY PALACE

They enter a hospital room where Jason lies in a bed, hooked up to machines. Joanna stands by his side, tears streaming down her face as she tells him she loves him.

JOANNA
(sobbing)
I remember this now, Charlie. I remember.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Back in the real world, Joanna sits on the couch, her eyes filled with tears as she holds a photograph of Jason.

JOANNA
(whispers)
Thank you, Charlie. I remember.

CHARLIE
(smiling)
You're welcome, Joanna.

As they leave the living room, they both know that they've been given a second chance to remember the past and cherish the memories of the ones they love.

FADE OUT.
